lessons.title: Clock Angles and Hand Speeds
lessons.concept: A clock is a circle of 360 degrees. The minute hand moves 360 degrees in 60 minutes (6 degrees per minute). The hour hand moves 360 degrees in 12 hours (30 degrees per hour or 0.5 degrees per minute). The angle between hands depends on both positions.
lessons.formula: Angle between hour and minute hands = |30*H - 5.5*M| degrees for time H:M (use smaller angle = min(angle, 360-angle) if required).
lessons.worked_example: Find the angle at 3:30. Using formula: |30*3 - 5.5*30| = |90 - 165| = 75 degrees. Intuitively, at 3:30 minute hand is at 6 (180 degrees from 12) and hour hand is halfway between 3 and 4 (105 degrees), difference 75 degrees.
mistakes: Assuming the hour hand stays exactly on the hour mark when minutes pass
Using 30*M instead of 5.5*M in the combined formula context
Not taking the smaller angle when the problem asks for it

lessons.title: Coincidence and Relative Motion of Hands
lessons.concept: Hands coincide (overlap) when they are at the same position. In 12 hours, minute and hour hands coincide 11 times (not 12) because the minute hand gains on the hour hand. The relative speed of minute hand with respect to hour hand is 5.5 degrees per minute.
lessons.formula: Relative speed = 6 - 0.5 = 5.5 degrees/minute. Time for gain of 360 degrees (one coincidence interval) = 360/5.5 = 720/11 = 65 5/11 minutes.
lessons.worked_example: Hands coincide at 12:00. Next coincidence is after 65 5/11 minutes, i.e., approximately 1:05 5/11. In a 12-hour period they coincide 11 times; in 24 hours, 22 times.
mistakes: Assuming hands coincide every hour (they do not, except the cycle count differs)
Forgetting relative speed and using only minute-hand speed
Confusing right angle occurrences with coincidence occurrences

lessons.title: Calendars and Odd Days
lessons.concept: Calendar problems use the concept of odd days: extra days beyond complete weeks. A normal year has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day. A leap year has 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 odd days. Leap years are generally years divisible by 4, except century years which must be divisible by 400.
lessons.formula: Odd days = total days mod 7. Leap year rule: divisible by 4 (and if century, divisible by 400). Day shifts forward by number of odd days.
lessons.worked_example: If today is Monday, after 10 days the day will be Monday + (10 mod 7) = Monday + 3 = Thursday. Year 2000 was a leap year (divisible by 400), 1900 was not (century year not divisible by 400), 2024 is a leap year (divisible by 4).
mistakes: Treating every year divisible by 4 as leap year including century exceptions
Counting total days but forgetting to reduce modulo 7
Off-by-one errors when counting days between dates

practice.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock at 3:00?
practice.explanation: At 3:00, minute hand is at 12 and hour hand is at 3. Each hour mark is 30 degrees (360/12), so difference = 3 * 30 = 90 degrees.

practice.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands at 6:30?
practice.explanation: Using |30H - 5.5M| = |30*6 - 5.5*30| = |180 - 165| = 15 degrees. Minute hand at 6 (180 degrees), hour hand halfway between 6 and 7 (195 degrees).
practice.provenance: Authored original practice item; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in 12 hours?
practice.explanation: The hands coincide once in every 65 5/11 minutes, so in 12 hours they coincide 11 times (they coincide at 12:00 but the 11:00-1:00 interval gives one coincidence at 12:00).

practice.question: How many odd days are there in a normal (non-leap) year?
practice.explanation: A normal year has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day. So it has 1 odd day.

practice.question: Which of the following years is a leap year?
practice.explanation: 2016 is divisible by 4, so it is a leap year. 1900 is a century year but not divisible by 400, so not a leap year. 2001 and 2010 are not divisible by 4.

questions.question: At what time between 5:00 and 6:00 will the hour and minute hands coincide?
questions.explanation: At 5:00, hour hand is at 150 degrees and minute hand at 0 degrees (gap 150 degrees). Relative speed = 5.5 degrees/minute. Time to coincide = 150/5.5 = 300/11 = 27 3/11 minutes. So hands coincide at 5:27 3/11.

questions.question: How many odd days are there in 100 years? (Assume the standard Gregorian pattern where 100 years contain 24 leap years and 76 ordinary years.)
questions.explanation: 76 ordinary years give 76 odd days and 24 leap years give 48 odd days, total = 124 odd days. 124 mod 7 = 5 (since 7*17=119, remainder 5).

questions.question: What is the angle between the hour and minute hands at 9:15?
questions.explanation: Angle = |30H - 5.5M| = |30*9 - 5.5*15| = |270 - 82.5| = 187.5 degrees. The smaller angle is 360 - 187.5 = 172.5 degrees. The question states 'the angle', and 172.5 degrees is the smaller (commonly asked) angle; option A matches this value.
